title: Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint denied. The SJC answered the stated issue 'No'—Pacific Presbytery did not err in denying Phelps's May 14, 2009 complaint. Pacific Presbytery's adoption of the Committee report finding no constitutional irregularities in Lee Irons's nomination, examination, election, and ordination as ruling elder stood. No remand or other relief; the NAPARC issue was expressly left undecided.
first_summary: Phelps complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by finding no constitutional irregularities in the NLB Session's ordination of Lee Irons as a ruling elder after PP declined to receive Irons as a teaching-elder candidate. The SJC affirmed PP's action, reasoning that great deference applies, that one office of elder does not require identical standards, and that the NLB Session had jurisdiction after Irons renounced OPC jurisdiction. The complaint was denied; the NAPARC issue was not decided.
summary: Phelps complained that Pacific Presbytery erred by finding no constitutional irregularities in the New Life Burbank Session's ordination of Lee Irons as a ruling elder, despite PP's earlier refusal to receive Irons as a teaching-elder candidate. The SJC denied the complaint. Under BCO 39-3.3, the Court owed great deference to the lower court's discretionary fitness judgment; the single office of elder does not require identical eligibility processes, and the NLB Session had jurisdiction after Irons renounced OPC jurisdiction. PP's action stood; the SJC declined to decide the NAPARC issue.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2009-24, Phelps v. Pacific Presbytery. SJC decision adopted 23 concurring, 1 disqualified, 0 absent (line 122). Facts by RE Cub Culbertson; issues, judgment, and reasoning by TE Fred Greco with SJC amendments (line 116).
evidence_notes.dispute: Phelps complained that PP erred by adopting a committee report finding no constitutional irregularities in the NLB Session's nomination, examination, election, and ordination of Lee Irons as ruling elder, despite PP's earlier denial of Irons's application as a teaching-elder candidate; PP denied the complaint on September 26, 2009 (lines 39–45, 49–51).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC denied the complaint and answered the issue 'No' (lines 53–55). Reason: BCO 39-3.3 gives great deference to a lower court on discretionary fitness judgments; the one office of ruling and teaching elder does not require identical eligibility processes; each court has discretion in admissions; and the NLB Session had jurisdiction after the OPC presbytery accepted Irons's renunciation (lines 59–114). No NAPARC ruling (line 112).
